doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Joining the Messengers and moving to New York
title: The single Messengers recording for Columbia
summary: The group records once, for a Dutch pianist's album, which Ware never heard.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: You never recorded with the Jazz Messengers, though?

Oh yes, we did. We recorded once. When we first got to New York. Columbia - Art was signed with Columbia then, and they had some young lady, she was Dutch; she was a vocalist, and I don't know know, Jutta Hipp or what her name was, but I never heard that album. But we made it and we got paid for it. So I don't know ... I never heard it. Donald Byrd, Ira Sullivan, Kenny Drew, myself, and Art Blakey.
Gee, I hope the tape is still around.

Well, they might have it on the shelf somewhere, or it might have been produced in Europe. You know, so who knows? It might come out one of these days, but I remember, that was the only time we recorded.
